leadIn:
I’m using the active settle workflow: first I’ll trace the renaming flow, tests, and repository conventions, then I’ll bring only genuinely user-owned behavior decisions through the native question form before changing code.

This is a **bounded** change: the existing single-directory rename flow in [src/rename.js](C:\Users\Ahmet\AppData\Local\Temp\groundwork-eval-settle-RD9qeF\src\rename.js) owns it; there is no new subsystem, API, or persistent format.

Verified facts:

- `applyRenames` renames sequentially, so an `EEXIST` leaves earlier steps applied (`src/rename.js`, comment and loop).
- The CLI prints the entire plan before applying it (`src/cli.js`).
- Matching is a sorted, one-time directory snapshot and includes every matching file (`src/match.js`); thus an occupied target may itself be a source scheduled to move.
- Undo and rename journals are explicitly excluded (`README.md`, “Out of scope”), while scripts and accidental repeat runs are established use cases.

**Inference:** “Fix this” could mean atomic refusal, skipping conflicts, or replacing files; those have materially different data-loss and script behavior. A second decision is how a concurrently changing directory should behave. Collision policy determines the implementation and tests; concurrency policy determines whether a valid newer file can be incorporated or must be left alone.

questions.question: When a target is occupied by a file that is not safely moving elsewhere in the same plan, what should the command do? A wrong choice risks either partial work or silent data loss; the current loop stops after earlier renames (`src/rename.js`).

options.label: Abort upfront (Recommended)
options.description: Validate the whole plan and make no changes; limitation: the user must clear the conflict and rerun.

options.label: Skip conflicts
options.description: Rename non-conflicting files and report skipped ones; limitation: numbering/output can contain gaps and the run is intentionally partial.

options.label: Replace targets
options.description: Overwrite conflicting target files and finish; limitation: existing data can be permanently lost.

questions.question: If another process adds or changes a relevant file after planning but while renaming, how should this run behave? A wrong choice can overwrite newer input or produce a mixed snapshot; scripts and a second invocation are plausible writers (`README.md`, “How it is used”).

options.label: Refuse overlap (Recommended)
options.description: Detect interference and fail without overwriting the newer input; limitation: coordination adds temporary on-disk bookkeeping during the run.

options.label: Finish snapshot
options.description: Complete only the names captured at startup while preserving unexpected files; limitation: the directory may reflect two interleaved runs.

options.label: Restart newer
options.description: Re-plan around the newest directory contents; limitation: numbering and printed plans can change during one invocation.

leadIn:
The first round settles two user-owned points:

- Collision probe → abort before changing anything.
- Concurrent probe → refuse overlapping runs.

More repository facts now matter:

- `cli.js` currently prints every planned rename before any validation, so a rejected run would otherwise emit success-looking stdout.
- Node filesystem operations can still fail after validation (permissions, removal, device errors); the repository has no rollback or transaction behavior today.
- `README.md` rules out persistent recovery state, but does not decide whether this invocation should attempt in-memory rollback.
- The existing test checks planning only; no executable acceptance check yet covers filesystem results (`test/rename.test.js`).

**Open tension:** upfront collision checks cure the reported case, but a later filesystem failure could still recreate the same partial-directory outcome. The failure-recovery choice determines staging/rollback behavior; output timing determines the CLI contract scripts observe.

questions.question: If a filesystem error occurs after renaming has begun despite preflight checks, what should remain? A wrong choice can recreate the complained-about partial state; no recovery contract exists in `README.md` or `src/rename.js`.

options.label: Roll back run (Recommended)
options.description: Restore names already moved and report failure; limitation: rollback itself can fail under severe external interference.

options.label: Leave progress
options.description: Stop and retain completed renames; limitation: the directory is partial, matching today’s rough edge.

questions.question: When preflight rejects a plan, should stdout still list the proposed renames? A wrong choice can make scripts interpret a failed run as completed work; `src/cli.js` currently prints before applying.

options.label: Print after success (Recommended)
options.description: Stdout describes only completed renames; limitation: users do not see the rejected proposal there.

options.label: Print proposal first
options.description: Preserve current plan-first stdout even on failure; limitation: scripts must use the exit code to distinguish proposals from completed work.

leadIn:
The frontier has three remaining observable cases:

- A replacement without `#` can assign the same destination to several sources; `planRenames` performs only one substitution and does not enforce uniqueness (`src/rename.js`).
- Running the same command twice is explicitly common (`README.md`), and the second plan can contain self-renames such as `photo-001.jpg → photo-001.jpg`.
- Refusing overlap needs a cross-process marker with Node built-ins; an abruptly killed process can leave that marker behind because the repository forbids a persistent journal but says nothing about stale coordination state.

**Inference:** duplicate destinations should probably be rejected under the same all-or-nothing rule, repeated no-op steps should probably be harmless, and dead-process markers should probably be reclaimed. These decisions affect validation, exit status, and crash recovery; after them, the full probe ledger can be closed.

questions.question: If multiple sources map to the same destination, what should happen? A wrong choice either makes the result order-dependent or rejects a malformed plan; `planRenames` permits this when the replacement lacks a varying `#` (`src/rename.js`).

options.label: Abort upfront (Recommended)
options.description: Reject the whole ambiguous plan with no changes; limitation: constant replacements cannot rename multiple files.

options.label: Keep first
options.description: Rename the first source and skip later duplicates; limitation: produces an intentionally partial result.

options.label: Keep last
options.description: Let the last source win; limitation: earlier source data may be replaced or displaced.

questions.question: When a repeated command produces source-to-same-name steps, how should those steps behave? A wrong choice makes the documented accidental second run either noisy or unsafe (`README.md`, “How it is used”).

options.label: No-op success (Recommended)
options.description: Treat already-correct names as completed and preserve a successful repeat; limitation: stdout may repeat unchanged mappings.

options.label: Reject self-renames
options.description: Fail before changes whenever any source already has its target name; limitation: accidental repeat runs fail.

questions.question: If a prior process died and left the overlap marker, what should the next run do? A wrong choice can either block renaming indefinitely or reclaim a marker while its owner still runs.

options.label: Reclaim if dead (Recommended)
options.description: Verify the recorded local PID is gone, then remove the marker; limitation: PID reuse is a small ambiguity.

options.label: Always refuse
options.description: Require manual marker removal after any crash; limitation: one killed run can block all later runs.

leadIn:
All eighteen probes are now closed. User-set closures are:

- Occupied external target → abort upfront.
- Valid newer input from an overlapping renamer → refuse overlap.
- Mid-run filesystem failure → roll back the run.
- Rejected-plan stdout → print nothing; print mappings only after success.
- Duplicate planned destinations → abort upfront.
- Repeated self-renames → no-op success.
- Dead owner’s coordination marker → reclaim it after verifying the local PID is gone.

Repository closures include: single-directory scope and basename confinement (`README.md`, `src/match.js`); no persistent journal or undo (`README.md`); sorted snapshot planning (`src/match.js`); stderr diagnostics/stdout user output (`AGENTS.md`); and the existing `planRenames` interface/test shape (`src/rename.js`, `test/rename.test.js`). No data migration or external schema can arise because state remains filesystem names plus a transient lock marker.

**Inference:** the resolved contract is an all-or-nothing rename transaction around the existing plan/apply seam: preflight every source and destination, serialize apply operations, stage moves safely (including destinations that are themselves moving), roll back on failure, and emit stdout only after commit. Focused filesystem tests plus the existing planning test will prove collision safety, chains, duplicate rejection, repeat behavior, and cleanup. Implementation waits only on confirmation that this contract is complete.

questions.question: Proceed with this contract: all-or-nothing same-directory renames; upfront rejection of occupied/duplicate targets; safe moves through planned-name chains; overlap refusal with dead-lock recovery; rollback on runtime failure; successful no-op repeats; stdout only after success; no undo, journal, recursion, skipping, or overwriting; prove it with focused Node filesystem tests. Is anything missing or wrong?

options.label: Implement it (Recommended)
options.description: Build and verify exactly this behavior; limitation: conflicting files must be cleared before rerunning.

options.label: Revise contract
options.description: Pause implementation so you can change a behavior or scope boundary; limitation: the reported bug remains unfixed for now.
